claims.text: In-situ TEM or STEM can elucidate mechanistic aspects of high-temperature oxidation in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
EDS coupled with in-situ TEM or STEM can elucidate elemental redistribution associated with nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
The investigated material is an Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy.
The Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy is produced by additive manufacturing.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure.
Nanoprecipitates are relevant structural mediators of oxidation behavior in this alloy.
Elemental redistribution is mechanistically connected to oxidation behavior.
In-situ TEM or STEM with EDS will improve understanding of nanoprecipitate evolution and elemental redistribution during oxidation relative to conventional characterization.
The proposed characterization is applicable under high-temperature oxidation conditions relevant to high-temperature applications.
The exact mechanisms of nanoprecipitate evolution and oxidation may be complex and influenced by multiple factors.
Comparing oxidation rate and nanoprecipitate evolution measured by in-situ microscopy against conventional characterization is a suitable test of the hypothesis.
A difference threshold of 10% in oxidation rate and 5% in nanoprecipitate evolution defines the proposed falsification decision.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats TEM/STEM-EDS as an observational method intended to provide greater mechanistic understanding, but the falsification rule expects the underlying oxidation rate and nanoprecipitate evolution to differ between characterization techniques. A characterization technique should not itself alter those material behaviors, so lack of a difference does not directly falsify its ability to resolve them.
